blocking_focus: Complete the candidate-bound Tester MCP state matrix.

preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `native_godot_project` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

Keep frozen technical baseline `host_godot_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Make the candidate ready for native 1920x1080 dense-wave qualification while delivering complete cemetery spatial integrity and a visibly authored, truthful upgrade-choice interface, preserving the intact environment package and frozen Godot boot baselines.

diagnosis.root_cause: The required dense-run check lacks qualifying native-renderer evidence because the bound environment uses llvmpipe; this is not proof of a new candidate defect. Candidate source also shows a secondary visibility-camera/compositor workaround after repeated arena camera treatments, so candidate-controlled rendering cost and landmark visibility remain coupled. The materially different strategy is authoritative wrapper/binding repair around the preserved cemetery instance, not more transform tuning. The upgrade draft has partial icon and projection infrastructure, but the hard same-loop capability still requires a complete player-facing choice hierarchy with explicit input-state acceptance.

stop_conditions: Do not claim the dense-performance gap passed from llvmpipe, editor idle, an empty arena, synthetic timing, or fewer than three qualifying native-renderer cycles.
Do not modify, split, duplicate, extract, hide, or reposition authored cemetery child meshes; preserve the accepted package, landmark anchors, navigation region, and package transform.
Stop and escalate if spatial integrity would require replacing the preserved cemetery package or destructively editing imported source assets.
Tester preparation actions must remain editor-only and absent from release input/export behavior; diagnostic setup cannot qualify an ordinary route.
Do not regress authoritative targeting, hit causality, telegraphs, pickups, upgrade transaction ordering, pause ownership, Retry cleanup, host Godot boot, or native project import.
Do not add a second full-world render pass, unbounded scene-tree scans, uncapped effects, or profiling work whose overhead invalidates the measured dense scenario.

strategy.rationale: Use the existing renderer-aware profiler rather than fabricating native evidence, remove candidate-controlled dense costs where demonstrated, replace repeated camera tuning with direct authored-instance wrapper/binding repair, and complete both required player-facing capabilities inside the single host-mandated task.

code: Run the frozen native Godot project and host boot checks; require clean import and launch with no fatal GDScript, resource, or scene errors.
Verify the cemetery remains one intact bound environment instance, imported sources are unchanged, and landmark, collision, navigation, spawn, and camera paths resolve.
Inspect the profiling contract for bounded histories, deterministic cycle identity, honest renderer gating, release guards, and absence of unbounded per-frame scene-tree or all-neighbor scans.
Validate every eligible upgrade projection binds an icon, emits only changed decision rows with at most three deltas, applies once, and matches authoritative post-choice state before unpausing.
runtime: Developer self-validation should exercise representative dense prepare, advance, and reset in the available renderer to prove density, content completeness, nonzero sampling, reset isolation, and clean runtime logs; software-renderer measurements remain diagnostic only.

GameLoop Runtime and Tester must recapture three complete native-renderer cycles at 1920x1080 with 25-40 ordinary enemies, Bellkeeper, all weapons, pickups, UI, animation, VFX, lights, and audio, then judge stable 60 FPS frame-time distribution and lifecycle growth.

Tester must replay ordinary movement against every side of the central building and each landmark and along the full perimeter, checking collision, navigation, visibility, disappearance, external depth, and legal enemy approach before contact, near contact, and after departure.

Tester must exercise a natural three-choice draft with keyboard, mouse, and gamepad; verify focus, hover, pressed, unavailable, newly unlocked, and selected states, hold confirm, apply one choice, and observe the advertised change in the next relevant combat event.
visual: Capture shipped-camera views at spawn, the loop and cross-route, each landmark before contact, near contact, and after departure, all four perimeter directions, a representative dense wave, and Bellkeeper combat. Reject visible void, primitive fill, whole-landmark disappearance, unstable occlusion, or blocked escape lanes.

Capture the upgrade draft at native viewport and representative windowed/UI-scale states for keyboard focus, mouse hover, gamepad focus, unavailable, newly unlocked, and selected cards. Confirm silhouette-first hierarchy, compact stat icons, truthful current-to-new values, restrained copy, and stable layout.

Compare representative runtime captures with the bound imagination reference for high-angle framing, coherent cemetery density, readable silhouettes, warm-versus-cool lighting, clear escape lanes, restrained effects, and compact HUD composition without copying its exact layout or trade dress.

done_when: The arena has a larger traversable scale than one camera-sized combat pad, with a readable loop and cross-route suitable for sustained ordinary movement.
A coherent non-playable external world extends beyond the collision perimeter in spawn, route, and cardinal gameplay views without reachable void, proxy-floor exposure, or unbounded spawn space.

The central building and every prominent landmark have aligned visible footprints, collision, navigation exclusion, spawn exclusion, and transform ownership; the player and representative enemies cannot pass through, enter, or become trapped inside them.

Before approach, at near contact, and after departure during ordinary movement, there is no whole-landmark disappearance, player concealment, dangerous-telegraph occlusion, or camera-occlusion drift. Any necessary transparency is selective, bounded, reversible, and never hides an entire landmark.
A complete boundary and perimeter movement replay verifies stable collision sliding, legal enemy approach, continuing external depth, and consistent landmark visibility on every side.

Normal and dense gameplay no longer depend on a secondary full-world visibility camera or compositor; the primary shipped camera remains responsive and keeps the Warden, nearby threats, and a useful escape direction readable.

The representative 1920x1080 profile resolves 25-40 ordinary enemies plus Bellkeeper, all three weapon families, pickups, HUD, animation, VFX, bounded lights, and audio, and records nonzero frame and physics samples, p50/p95/p99 frame-time distributions, draw calls, high-water marks, renderer identity, and runtime errors.

Dense work is bounded through stable caps, pooling, cached registries, spatial queries, or deterministic staggered presentation without delaying authoritative telegraphs, accepted hits, damage, death, drops, or legal target changes. Three prepare/advance/reset cycles carry distinct provenance and return active actors, transients, audio, pause state, UI state, signals, timers, and warmed pools to,.
tasks.instructions:
Implement one release-convergence task with three required sub-surfaces.

Dense performance: use the existing renderer-aware profile to identify and repair candidate-controlled costs. Preserve honest renderer classification, record samples even when the renderer is ineligible, and keep software-renderer results explicitly non-qualifying. Prefer removal of redundant rendering and bounded lifecycle work over more telemetry. Preserve ordinary balance, pooling traces, spawner safe-distance validation, WaveDirector route tracking, and immediate authoritative combat events.

Arena spatial integrity: use direct instance restoration, wrapper/binding repair, or explicit selective isolation instead of repeating transform tuning. Keep the accepted cemetery as one intact authoritative environment instance. Expand only the product-owned traversable datum needed for a larger traversable scale; align its external world, central building and landmark collision, navigation and spawn exclusion, boundary and perimeter, and primary-camera containment. Do not replace native streets with PlaneMesh roads, patches, facade slices, or backdrops. Verify disappearance and occlusion through ordinary movement and movement replay around every landmark and the full perimeter.

Upgrade choices: replace any remaining text-stacked presentation with an authored choice visual hierarchy. Lead every weapon or upgrade option with recognizable silhouettes or icons, then show truthful current-to-new values for no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas. Never show NEW or LOCKED as a CURRENT value, and omit unchanged, exhaustive, unavailable, or unrelated rows. Keep copy restrained and provide complete keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus, plus distinct hover, pressed, unavailable, newly unlocked, and selected states without changing card dimensions. A held confirm must apply exactly one authoritative choice before gameplay resumes, and the next relevant combat event must reflect the advertised change.
